componentPlan.focusQuote: the value of one variable in a problem depends uniquely on the value of another variable in the problem
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Checks recall of function dependence and sine cosine tangent relationships

componentPlan.focusQuote: We are going to use the cosine of the angle in this example, but a similar example could be made using the sine or the tangent.
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Walks through black to red to blue triangle scaling to show cosine stays constant

overview.headline: Functions link variables uniquely, shown by constant cosine ratios in similar triangles

keyPoints.point: A function means one variable depends uniquely on another variable in a problem
keyPoints.quote: the value of one variable in a problem depends uniquely on the value of another variable in the problem

keyPoints.point: trigonometric sine cosine and tangent relate sides and angles of a triangle
keyPoints.quote: The trigonometric functions sine, cosine, and tangent relate the various sides and angles of a triangle.

keyPoints.point: Cosine of angle b is adjacent divided by hypotenuse and stays same when sides double or triple
keyPoints.quote: Dividing out the “2’s” gives x divided by y, the same value as the black triangle.

keyPoints.point: Tables of sine cosine and tangent let us solve for unknown sides and angles
keyPoints.quote: If we know the length of any one side, we can solve for the length of the other sides.

keyTerms.gloss: dependence fixed by angle rather than side length
keyTerms.quote: Scientists call this type of dependence a function.

keyTerms.gloss: ratio of adjacent side to hypotenuse fixed by angle
keyTerms.quote: because the ratio of x to y, (x/y), is defined to be the cosine of “b” and this value is fixed by “b”.

keyTerms.gloss: longest side whose length is y in smallest triangle
keyTerms.quote: The black triangle is the smallest triangle and has a hypotenuse “h” of length “y” and an adjacent side “a” equal to “x”.

keyTerms.gloss: side forming angle whose ratio to hypotenuse gives cosine
keyTerms.quote: The ratio of the adjacent side to the hypotenuse is a function of the angle “b”.

keyTerms.gloss: relation using a variable as repeated multiplier
keyTerms.quote: The exponential function relates a variable to the number of times another variable is used as a multiplier

analysis.pageCoverage: Page introduces the idea of function as unique dependence between variables, defines exponential, logarithmic and trigonometric functions, and demonstrates with scaled right triangles that cosine depends only on angle, with tables to solve sides and angles.
